subject: Unable to change global variables from within trajectories

messages.author: 7f8cd4ac6e742852
messages.subject: Unable to change global variables from within trajectories
parts:
Hi,

This problem seems like it should be pretty basic but I have tried a number of different things and nothing seems to work, at least not when it's included in a trajectory.

I simply want to change the value of a global variable from within a trajectory:

trajectory("pericarditis") %>%
                            branch(function() sample(c(1,2), size=1, replace=T, prob = c(attr_peri,(1-attr_peri))), continue=c(T),
                                trajectory("prev_peri") %>%
                                  seize("peri_dummy", 1) %>%
                                  seize("periec", 1) %>%
                                  seize("perieq", 1) %>%
                                  seize("periogc", 1) %>%
                                  seize("periogq", 1) %>% 
                                  timeout(flare_length),
                               
                                  trajectory("new_peri") %>%
                                  seize("peri_dummy", 1) %>%
                                  seize("periec", 1) %>%
                                  seize("perieq", 1) %>%
                                  seize("periogc", 1) %>%
                                  seize("periogq", 1) %>% 
                                  timeout(flare_length) %>%
                                  attr_peri <- 1

The idea is that the first arrival in the "pericarditis" trajectory goes down the "new_peri" trajectory then, by updating the attr_peri variable from 0 to 1 and thereby adjusting the probabilities, all of the next arrivals go down the "prev_peri" trajectory.

I must be missing something in how simmer works, or maybe there is an easier way to do this?

Many thanks in advance,
Tray

messages.subject: Re: [simmer-devel] Unable to change global variables from within trajectories
parts:
Hi Iñaki,

Thank you again for getting back to me.

I have tried using set_global and get_global previously in the following code:

env <- simmer()

set <- trajectory("set") %>%
  set_global(keys = "attri_peri", 0)

cvman <- trajectory("cvman") %>% 
  
  branch(function() sample(c(1,2), size=1, replace=T, prob = c(0.9,0.1)), continue=c(T),
         trajectory("no_cvman") %>%
           seize("no_cvman_dummy", 1) %>%
           timeout(1),
         trajectory("yes_cvman") %>%
           seize("cvman_dummy", 1) %>%
                   branch(function() sample(c(1,2), size=1, replace=T, prob = c((1-prob_peri),prob_peri)), continue=c(T),
                          trajectory("no_pericarditis") %>%
                            seize("no_peri_dummy", 1) %>%
                            timeout(task = 1),
branch(function() sample(c(1,2), size=1, replace=T, prob = c(function() get_attribute("attri_peri"), function() 1 - get_attribute("attri_peri"))), continue=c(T),

timeout(flare_length) %>%
                                  activate("tamp_patient") %>%
                                  set_source("tamp_patient", function () time_to_tamp) %>%
                                  set_global(keys = "attri_peri", 1)
                          )
                   )
  )

But that would get me the following error: "Evaluation error: (list) object cannot be coerced to type 'double'" which I understood as meaning that get_global was not returning a numeric value. This is why I was trying different methods.

Am I using get_global incorrectly?

Many thanks,
Tray
